angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 591,345 km at 175.92 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.6844 +/- 0.0092 mas (same row, RUWE 0.80): 175.92 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.85 +/- 0.025 solar radii from Morton et al. 2016, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of Kepler-1313 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...822...86M/abstract): 591,345 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.92 +/- 0.031 solar masses from Morton et al. 2016, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of Kepler-1313 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...822...86M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5453 +/- 82.15 K from Morton et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-1313 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...822...86M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Morton et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-1313 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...822...86M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/kepler-1313.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.543, rounded to two decimals
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, Kepler-1313: main object type Er*, Eruptive Variable
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-1313 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0 dex, from Morton et al. 2016 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...822...86M/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-1313 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.3248, from Gajdoš et al. 2019 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019RAA....19...41G/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-1313 (pscomppars): age 2.69 Gyr, from Morton et al. 2016 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...822...86M/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: VizieR J/ApJ/807/170/table2 (Prograde vs retrogade motions. II. KOIs), column Prot: 6.14 d, the row 0.1 arcsec from the star's J2000 place. The middle of 24 catalogued periods, 24 of them within 20% of it
